name: tuong_chua_kito_vua
sources: The statue of Christ the King on Núi Nhỏ (Tao Phùng), Vũng Tàu (Tượng Chúa Kitô Vua, Chúa giang tay). The monument is 32 m high: a base of 6 m, a dome of 3 m, the figure of 22 m from its soles to the top of its halo, and a lightning rod of 1 m. 18.4 m from fingertip to fingertip; a hand of 2.2 m; 133 steps inside (the site of the pilgrimage centre, kitovungtau.com, the history page).

Made of reinforced concrete, cast in place in 1974 and 1975, finished in 1992 to 1994. The model and the reliefs: the sculptor Văn Nhân; the concrete: the engineer Nguyễn Quảng Đức. The robe and the hair are washed stone; the face, the hands, the feet and the heart are white ground stone (kitovungtau.com; vi.wikipedia.org, Tượng Chúa Kitô Vua (Vũng Tàu)).

The heights and the widths between those sizes are measured on photos of Wikimedia Commons (Category:Christ of Vũng Tàu: the front view by trungydang, CC BY 3.0, with the three windows for its perspective), each in about 0.2 m. The measures of plan 0005 (priv/measures/tuong_chua_kito_vua), with 18.4 m from fingertip to fingertip, agree in 0.5 m.

The halo goes round the head and leans to the front by 30 degrees (the measure of plan 0005, and the close photos). A guess from photos: the depths (one side view from below), the plan of the base, the face, the marks of the windows. The reliefs of the base are panels with no figures.

The inside, at the near level: a room in the base with its door at the back, the dome, and a stair of 133 steps round a post up to the floor of the shoulders and the two balconies; six windows with grilles. The sources give the 133 steps, the door at the back and the windows; the walls (0.25 to 0.4 m), the post and the plan of the room are a guess.
It is from edits only, in parts: each part is a sculpture with its own cells and its own image (plan 0014).
